My family’s story is uniquely American. Now more than ever, we need to fight to keep that promise alive for the next generation.

Donald Trump and Xi Jinping will meet in Washington this week. It’s critical that President Trump use this moment to secure increased AI safety coordination on the shared risks that frontier models hold, while also confronting China’s calculated efforts to overtake the U.S. in the AI development race.

Frontier AI models are developing faster than experts ever believed possible, with safety risks that researchers, industry and governments alike agree could hold existential threats. We need formalized international coordination and communication — with China and other countries — to ensure the push to develop and diffuse the most capable AI models does not cause catastrophic consequences for humanity.

China also has a long record of stealing American technological advancements and intellectual property — including through distillation attacks in which Chinese AI labs train models on America’s advanced AI models and then use those increased capabilities to threaten our national security. Trump must hold Xi to account for this blatant theft. 

Finally, Trump should reverse course on selling advanced chips to China. These chips give us advantages in safety and computing power to outcompete China in AI development — and selling them to China only squanders the leverage and innovation advantage that we have developed here in the U.S. Since we are concerned that China will not pace its development of AI to ensure its safety, we should not be selling China the chips to make that prospect even more likely. If Trump refuses to withhold sensitive technology from China, I’m hopeful that Congress will.

We are in a moment of great technological transformation and upheaval. Federal inaction is not an option. The U.S. must seize this opportunity for international leadership in protecting against AI’s gravest risks.
